2610.05305.title: Characterizing Parallelism Strategies in LLM Inference: Fundamental Compute-Communication Trade-offs
2610.05305.paper_summary: Large Language Model (LLM) inference has become the dominant workload in modern AI systems, requiring serving infrastructures to maximize throughput while meeting strict latency Service-Level Objectives (SLOs). Since state-of-the-art LLMs exceed the compute and memory capacity of a single GPU, inference is commonly distributed across multiple GPUs using tensor parallelism (TP), pipeline parallelism (PP), or hybrid parallelism (HB). However, selecting the most effective parallelism strategy remains challenging due to complex interactions among computation, communication, pipeline utilization, sequence length, batch size, and model architecture. Existing approaches largely rely on empirical evaluation and provide limited analytical insight into the trade-offs among these strategies, particularly across the distinct prefill and decoding phases of inference. In this paper, we present a unified analytical framework for modeling distributed LLM inference under TP, PP, and HB. The framework decomposes end-to-end latency into computation, inter-GPU communication, and pipeline bubble overhead, and derives analytical models that capture TP collective communication, PP point-to-point communication, and pipeline utilization as functions of hardware, model, and workload characteristics. The model further characterizes the differing execution behavior of prefill and decoding, explaining why PP-oriented configurations favor compute-intensive prefill while TP-oriented configurations reduce decoding latency by eliminating pipeline bubbles. Experiments with modern LLMs on multi-GPU platforms validate the model and confirm the fundamental compute-communication trade-off across parallelism strategies. The framework provides practical guidance for parallelism selection, capacity planning, and optimization of future LLM serving systems.
2610.05305.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型 (LLM) 推論已成為現代 AI 系統中的主導工作負載，要求服務基礎設施在滿足嚴格的延遲服務水平目標 (SLO) 的同時最大化吞吐量。由於最先進的 LLM 超過了單個 GPU 的計算和記憶體容量，因此推論通常使用張量並行 (TP)、管道並行 (PP) 或混合並行 (HB) 在多個 GPU 之間分配。然而，選擇最有效的並行策略仍然具有挑戰性，因為計算、通信、管道利用率、序列長度、批次大小和模型架構之間存在複雜的相互作用。現有的方法在很大程度上依賴於經驗評估，並對這些策略之間的權衡提供有限的分析洞見，特別是在推論的不同預填充和解碼階段之間。在本文中，我們提出了一個統一的分析框架，用於建模在 TP、PP 和 HB 下的分佈式 LLM 推論。該框架將端到端延遲分解為計算、GPU 之間的通信和管道氣泡開銷，並推導出捕捉 TP 集體通信、PP 點對點通信和管道利用率的分析模型，這些模型是硬體、模型和工作負載特徵的函數。該模型進一步描述了預填充和解碼的不同執行行為，解釋了為什麼以 PP 為導向的配置偏向於計算密集型的預填充，而以 TP 為導向的配置則通過消除管道氣泡來減少解碼延遲。在多 GPU 平台上對現代 LLM 的實驗驗證了該模型，並確認了並行策略之間的基本計算-通信權衡。該框架為並行性選擇、容量規劃和未來 LLM 服務系統的優化提供了實用指導。
2610.05305.author: Javad Mirzaei et.al.
